text: AWS draws one line everywhere: AWS is responsible for security of the cloud, and you're responsible for security in the cloud. It's the single most-tested concept on every AWS certification.

AWS secures the facilities, hardware, host OS, and network backbone. You secure everything you configure on top: IAM, OS patching where it applies, firewall rules, encryption, and bucket access settings.
That line slides with how much AWS manages. On EC2 you patch the guest OS yourself; on RDS, AWS patches the database engine; on S3, there's no OS at all, but bucket policy is entirely yours.
Most real AWS security incidents are exactly this: a misconfigured bucket, squarely on the customer's side. Next up: IAM basics, where that work actually happens.
